Model series: Stereo Collection — a new family of snowboards for 2027 [3] 5. Product type: Snowboard [2] 6. Board category: Freestyle–All Mountain [2] 7. Gender: Men's [2] 8. Manufacturer: Bataleon Snowboards, headquartered in Amsterdam, Netherlands [4] 9. Parent company: Nidecker Group (NDK Group), a family-owned Swiss company that acquired Low Pressure Studio (Bataleon, Lobster, Switchback) in 2018 [5] 10. Founder: Jørgen Karlsen, Norwegian biophysicist, founded Bataleon in 2000 [6] 11. Co-founders/operators: Dennis Dusseldorp and Danny Kiebert have run Bataleon from Amsterdam for close to two decades [7] 12. Manufacturing location: Austria — currently manufactured at CAPiTA MFG ("The Mothership"), Feistritz a.d. Gail, Austria [8] 13. Manufacturing history: Previously produced at the Elan factory in Feistritz, Austria; temporarily outsourced to Asia after Elan went bankrupt; moved all production to CAPiTA MFG from the 14/15 season onward [9] 14. Brand heritage: Over 20 years of 3D snowboard tech with patented Triple Base Technology™ [10] 15. Industry position: NDK Group (parent) is considered the second biggest snowboard company in the world [11] 16. Brand reputation: Bataleon has "experienced steady, healthy growth over the past few years" per Global Director of Marketing Tom Johnson [12] 17. Model debut: The Stereo is a brand-new model family for the 2026/27 season — first year available [13] 18. Stereo collection description: "A family of snowboards that introduces both a new construction approach and an evolution of 3-dimensional shaping" [14] 19. Related model (upgrade): Stereo Team — upgraded team-driven version with stiffer flex (6/10), Light Core, C.S.T. SuperTubes, and Ultra Glide S base [15] 20. Related model (women's): Bataleon Women's Stereo — same construction/technology, adapted sizing [16] 21. Pro rider input: Developed with input from Bataleon Pro Rider Ethan Morgan [2] 22. Pro rider input (Stereo collection): Stereo family inspired by years of riding and innovation with Ethan Morgan and Halldór Helgason [17] 23. Stereo collection positioning per Boardsport SOURCE: "Stereo Collection (Stereo Team is a joint Pro Model with Ethan Morgan & Halldór Helgason) — An all-new family of models from Bataleon" [18] 24. 26/27 season focus: Bataleon's leading focus for 26/27 is "the in-tune freestyle audience" with expanded twin and directional twin range [19] 25. Market trend context: "The 24/25 season showed that the demand was especially strong for twin freestyle boards, driven by younger riders" [20] 26. Flex rating: 4/10 (Medium-soft) [2][21] 27. Shape: Twin (symmetrical, identical tip and tail) — 3D Twin [2][21] 28. Camber type: Medium Camber with 3BT and SideKick 2.0, Low Nose Sidebase Uplift and Low Tail Sidebase Uplift [2] 29. Base technology: Triple Base Technology (3BT) — reduces risk of edge-catch while maintaining ollie power and carving control [2] 30. SideKick 2.0: Amplifies sidebase uplift beyond widest points of nose and tail for hull-like shape, enhanced float, improved turn initiation [2] 31. Sidecut type: Tri-radial [2] 32. Width options: Standard, Wide [2] 33. Mounting system: 2x4 Inserts [2] 34. Laminate: Bi-Ax fiberglass with Carbon Stringers [2] 35. Carbon reinforcement: Carbon stringers strategically placed to fine-tune flex, response, and overall feel [2] 36. Core: Core Core — full poplar core reinforced with two hardwood beech stringers [2] 37. Sidewall material: Flex Walls — Urethane sidewalls instead of ABS, bonds more effectively to core, more durable and damp [2] 38. Base: Hyper Glide S — standard sintered base, fast and durable [2] 39. Construction: HyCap Construction — durable polyurethane sidewalls in tip and tail for impact resistance, full cap through contact length for reduced weight and enhanced edge grip [2] 40. Terrain: Freestyle, All Mountain, park [2] 41. Rider level: Intermediate [2] 42. Riding style description: Quick, agile, highly responsive; hunting new lines through the park [2] 43. Available lengths: 150cm, 152cm, 154cm, 156cm, 158cm, 156cm Wide, 159cm Wide [2] 44. NOTE on size discrepancy: Merchant lists 153W in detailed specs but lists 156W in available lengths; manufacturer site also lists 153W. The correct Wide sizes appear to be 153W, 156W, 159W [2] 45. Bi-Ax fiberglass description: "A traditional two-way weave that is light, strong and playful; it keeps the board snappy without adding torsional stiffness" [22] 94. 3BT technology principle: "At the heart of every Bataleon is a combination of 3BT™ and positive camber…minimizes the potential for edge-catch without sacrificing ollie power or carving performance" [23] 95. HyCap construction detail: "Full cap construction through the contact length for energy and precision, with durable polyurethane sidewalls at the tip and tail for added impact resistance" [14] 96. HyCap construction — new to Bataleon: This is described as "a brand-new Bataleon construction approach" [24] 97. Flex Walls description: "Urethane sidewalls provide smoother turn entry, improved chatter absorption, and enhanced durability in cold temperatures" [25] 98. SideKick 2.0 mechanism: "Dramatically increases the sidebase uplift just outside the widest points of the nose and tail" [23] 99. 3BT user experience (forum): "The 3bt makes the boards feel very catch-free and comfortable while retaining the power of full camber" [26] 100. 3BT user experience (forum — negative): "The downside is it can feel a little loose in firm snow compared to traditional boards. Not as strong with edge hold in icy snow." [27] 101. Camber profile: Traditional positive camber from tip to tail, combined with 3BT 3D shaping in the sidebases [28] 102. Stereo flex: 4/10 (medium-soft); Stereo Team flex: 6/10 (medium) [21][29] 103. Stereo core: Core Core — full poplar core reinforced with two hardwood beech stringers [2]; Stereo Team core: Light Core — lightweight 2:2 Poplar/Paulownia blend [30] 104. Stereo base: Hyper Glide S (standard sintered) [2]; Stereo Team base: Ultra Glide S — "A premium, 7000-grade sintered base reserved for high-end models" [31] 105. Stereo Team additional feature: C.S.T. SuperTubes — "Central Super Tube, a single Super Tube down the middle of the board enhances pop without stiffening the board torsionally" [32] 106. Stereo Team additional feature: Impact Plates — "Reinforced zones beneath the binding inserts reduce the risk of compression damage" [33] 107. Stereo rider level: Intermediate [2]; Stereo Team rider level: Intermediate to advanced [15] 108. Stereo Team position: "The upgraded team-driven version of the Stereo — built for riders who want more power, more pop and pro-level freestyle performance" [15] 109. Ride description (S2AS): "Blends freestyle creativity with all-mountain capability, delivering playful control and dependable response" [21] 110. Park capability: "Built as a true 3D Twin, the Stereo offers balanced park performance with enough stability for carving groomers and charging side hits" [34] 111. Progression: "Smooth, energetic and progression-ready, it's a board that keeps sessions fun across the whole resort" [34] 112. Carbon stringers benefit: "Added snap and energy return" [21] 113. Bi-Ax Laminate + Flex Walls feel: "Smooth torsional flex with added resilience" [35] 114. 3BT freestyle benefit (from Bataleon): "Our ability to refer to 3BT as a 'get-out-of-jail-free' card, helping to land tricks where your precision might not be 100%" [36] 115. 3BT powder benefit (forum): "3BT…helps the board float better in soft snow and has the feeling of rolling smoothly from edge to edge" [37] 116. 3BT concern on ice (forum user): "I've heard 3bt is bad on ice" — some forum users report reduced edge hold on hard/icy snow [38] 117. Soft flex advantage (Bataleon): "Softer snowboards are easier to press and won't kick your ass if you make a mistake" [39] 118. Price (AUD, merchant-listed): AUD $939.99 [2] 119. Availability (merchant): Preorder, estimated availability May 1, 2026 [2] 120. Shipping restriction (merchant): Only available for shipping within Australia [2] 121. Stereo Team availability (eBay/Boarderline Insanity): Available via eBay and vtsnowboarder.com from Boarderline Insanity [48] 130. Bataleon.com (Official): Direct-to-consumer official webshop; free shipping over $50, 45-day returns [49] 131. Surface 2 Air Sports (S2AS): UK-based authorised Bataleon retailer with price match guarantee; ships internationally [50] 132. Darkside Snowboards: US-based (Vermont) specialty snowboard shop; $629.99 for Stereo Team [41] 133. Blauer Board Shop: US-based specialty retailer stocking Bataleon [51] 134. Exodus Ride Shop: US-based retailer; $629.95 for Stereo Team [42] 135. Ski Pro AZ: US-based retailer; $629.95 for Stereo Team [43] 136. The Source Snowboard & Skate: Retailer with 30-day return/exchange policy; $564.00 for Stereo Team (sold out) [52] 137. People Skate and Snowboard: US-based retailer carrying Stereo Team [53] 138. Boarderline Insanity (vtsnowboarder.com / eBay): Family-owned Vermont shop, in business since early 2000s, 100% positive eBay feedback, 120K+ items sold [48] 139. Behind The Pines: Amsterdam-based specialty snowboard shop — carried limited 2026 Stereo Team [54] 140. Warranty: 2 year limited warranty against manufacturing defects from original date of purchase from Authorized Dealer [55] 141. Extended warranty: 2+1 year warranty (3 years) available when product is registered and customer subscribed to newsletter [56] 142. Returns (Bataleon direct): 45-day return policy [49] 143. Warranty experience (forum): Some forum users have reported mixed warranty experiences, including delamination issues being initially handled with voucher offers rather than replacement [57] 144. Bomb Hole Podcast review: Seth Huot reviewed the Stereo Team for the Bomb Proof series (February 2, 2026); examined the 3BT base contour paired with tri-radial sidecut and SideKick technology [58] 145. Boardsport SOURCE preview: Stereo collection featured in the F/W 2026/27 Retail Buyer's Guide, described as an "all-new family of models from Bataleon" [18] 146. Note: No independent on-snow review of the standard Men's Stereo (non-Team) was found at the time of this research — the model is brand-new and still on preorder. The Bomb Hole review covers the Stereo Team only. [Unverified — based on absence of evidence] 147. In-brand comparable (softer freestyle): Bataleon Evil Twin — true twin, medium flex (5/10), classic freestyle twin for park-first riders [59] 148. In-brand comparable (all-mountain): Bataleon Goliath — directional twin, all-mountain focus, stiffer flex [60] 149. In-brand comparable (park/jib): Bataleon Whatever — directional twin, playful, sub-mid flex [61] 150. Evil Twin vs Stereo positioning: The Stereo appears to replace/supplement the Evil Twin's niche as Bataleon's primary freestyle twin, but with the new HyCap construction and evolved 3BT/sidecut [13] 151. Cross-brand competitor: CAPiTA Horrorscope (freestyle twin, similar soft flex, park-focused) 152. Cross-brand competitor: Ride Twinpig (freestyle twin, medium-soft flex) 153. Cross-brand competitor: Burton Process (all-mountain freestyle twin) 154. 3BT general user sentiment (forum — positive): "I love the 3bt and find no issues with it although some do" [62] 155. 3BT general user sentiment (forum — mixed): "Some riders really don't like it. But I really like it generally unless the snow is pretty bad" [63] 156. 3BT positive: "It makes it feel really safe to try spins and mess around in general" [64] 157. Bataleon unique selling proposition: "We have never made a snowboard without a 3D base because we believe it is the key to more fun and better performance on the mountain" [65] 158. Stance position: Centered inserts [2] 159. Flex direction: True twin — symmetrical flex [2] 160. Setback: Zero (centered/twin) [2] 161. Taper: None (true twin) [2] 162. Base type: Sintered (Hyper Glide S — standard sintered) [2] 163. Fiberglass configuration: Bi-axial [2] 164. Edge material: Standard steel (no special edge tech mentioned) [2] 165. Binding compatibility: Standard 2x4 insert pattern — compatible with all standard snowboard bindings [2] 166. Manufacturing quality note: Whitelines states "All Bataleon boards are hand-built in Austria at the Mothership with focus on craftsmanship and exceptional materials" [66] 167. Snowleader on durability: "Boards manufactured in Europe, specifically in Austria, ensuring proven durability" [67] 168. Bataleon design language: "Known for eye-catching graphics and high-quality construction, contributing to their reputation as a premium snowboard brand" [68]
